A friend bought this ice maker for me after the one in my freezer died. I've owned it for about 2 weeks. My plan was to make ice and store it in the dispenser in my freezer. There is one issue. These cubes are stored at just about freezing, so they are a bit "wet". If I empty the basket directly into my dispenser, they freeze into one big lump. So I take the little basket of ice and put it in my freezer, then bounce it around to separate the cubes and load them into the dispenser. This works pretty well and gives me really cold cubes, which do a better job of cooling my drinks and don't dilute them as much.
Can't get away from the "wet ice" syndrome, as the ice is stored on the same compartment as the not-yet-frozen water. There is no temperature control, and if there were, the water would freeze before it could be made into cubes.

I purchased this product the 6/1/76. I've had ti running 24/7 once it arrived.
As w/ anything mechanical they never run forever and not have its problems.
First up. As w/ anything involving water. It's going for lack of a better word get 'GUNK' build up. Even if using filtered water which is highly recommended. I surmise this happens due to water recycling.
The walls of the water reservoir and water trough need to be cleaned of GUNK on a monthly basis of run 24/7 as I do run mine.
Most times all I clean it out w/ is paper towels held fast w/ a Hemostat. To get in between the refrigerating thingies that produce the ice.
A word of CAUTION at this point. Do not use any material that will leave some of itself (I.e.) LINT behind.
Lint leads me to my first problem w/ this unit. Plugged up the water outlet that fills the water trough & caused the water to miss the trough by redirecting the water coming from the water outlet that fills the trough. I had to remove it's outer back panel & top in order to remove the lint blockage from the water outlet. The second problem is that the sensor that shuts down the unit when the basket is full has stopped doing it's thing. Minor problems that I or anyone else can overcome w/ a little resourcefulness. All in all, I say this icemaker is a very good buy. But that is up to the individual to ponder.

I read many reviews of countertop ice makers before deciding on this Della model. It is true that the cubes (well, they're technically not cube-shaped but rather come out of the machine like cute little hollow igloos;) do melt pretty quickly if you don't transfer them to a freezer as soon as the inside ice basket is full.
Moreover, I find that they will clump together once they freeze up a bit more (as some reviewers stated) but a couple of whacks of the bag they're in breaks them up easily. So that's no big deal for me personally.
One thing I have noted is that when the ice maker has run though all its cycles (about 4-6 if I fill it to maximum level using four 16.9 fl. oz. of bottled water), there's still quite a lot of water left in the reservoir in spite of the ADD WATER indicator turning on.
It seems a waste of water but I suppose the remainder can be recycled back into original plastic bottle & used again.
Again, not a big problem in the long run.
All this to say, the hot & humid summer weather we've been experiencing in the Northeast has been much more bearable because of this efficient & easy-to-operate ice-maker!
